subject: On-prem VPC blueprint: control/data plane failover & observability sync
messages:
From: Alicia Chen <alicia.chen@novarasys.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 16:05:00 -0400
Subject: Novara on-prem VPC kickoff: topology requirements and questions

Hi Kim / team —

Thanks again for agreeing to run a short architecture sync on Novara's private deployment needs. Attached is a one‑page summary of our mandatory constraints, but summarizing the key asks so you have context: 

- Control plane: must be reachable from our colo via IPsec VPN, control API endpoints behind an ALB equivalent, mTLS + client certs for RPCs. No public control-plane endpoints.
- Data plane: dedicated tenant overlay (L2/L3 demarc via VLANs), egress strictly via our customer egress proxy (we cannot allow direct internet egress from inference nodes).
- KV/Cache state: we must preserve model KV-caches for warm-start across short interruptions; acceptable handshake pattern is a persisted redis-cluster in our tenancy or a mirrored cache bridge.
- Observability: distributed traces + tokenized metrics forwarded to our telemetry endpoint; sample rate targets: 1% tokens sampled, span latencies under 5ms for control-plane RPCs.
- SLA: baseline 99.9% for inference path, 99.95% for control plane. RTO expectations for control plane failovers: <5min to reach degraded read-only state.

Could you confirm a) whether Redwood can support the persisted KV-cache mirror pattern without opening outbound egress to public caches, b) an initial failover plan (single colo to colo DR) and c) a rough cut of the network demarc diagram?

I've attached novara-vpc-reqs.pdf (short) and proposed times for a 60m call later this week. 

Thanks —
Alicia Chen
Engineering Manager, Integrations
Novara Systems

Subject: Re: Novara on-prem VPC kickoff: topology requirements and questions

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear summary and the doc. We reviewed the requirements and sketched an initial blueprint (attached) describing control/data boundaries and the proposed failover matrix. High-level notes: 

- KV-cache mirror: we can implement a mirrored cache bridge that lives in your tenant and accepts connections from Redwood inference nodes over a pinned VPN tunnel. This avoids public egress and keeps the cache within your network. The bridge will present a Redis-compatible front-end; write-through semantics during failover will be the default.
- Control plane: we propose a private control-plane VIP reachable over the IPsec fabric. Control-plane services run in a small, isolated management VPC; they authenticate with mutual TLS and a short-lived token issued by your KMS.
- Data-plane: inference pods stay in a separate tenant VLAN and only egress through your egress proxy. We'll use a local sidecar for metrics forwarding that relays to your telemetry endpoint over an authenticated channel.
- Failover behavior: primary/secondary colo pair with active-passive for control-plane state. On detection of primary failure, we promote the secondary and flip a BGP announcement; redis mirror stays writable on secondary. We'll include a canary routing policy to avoid full traffic shifts until KV sync is validated.

I've attached two artifacts: kimberly-vpc-proposal-20280710.pdf (proposal with sequence diagrams) and runtime-seg-diag-v1.png (network demarc sketch). We're targeting a design review call on Thu 07/11 at 10:00 AM PT. Can you confirm?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Kim / Alicia — couple of operational caveats from the runtime team that we should call out in the design review: 

- KV-cache durability: mirrored write-through helps, but during a control-plane flip we need to ensure the KV cache client on the inference node can atomically switch to a read-only mode if sync is behind. Otherwise we'll expose stale model state. Suggest we add a 'cache-consistency' probe in the canary that validates per-shard r/w before promoting.
- Telemetry and cost: forwarding span-level traces for every request at 1% sampling is fine, but we need to validate tokenization so no PII is forwarded. Ops-runbook-checklist.md attached includes gating checks (PII scrub, token hashes only).
- Latency: if your colo pair is cross-region we should quantify tail latency impact on KV-sync; a semi-synchronous replication may be required with stronger staleness controls.

Also, Jonas: can you add the proposed rollout/rollback commands to the runbook (especially the BGP flip procedure and the control-plane read-only switch)? 

On the review call: let's allocate 15min to the canary procedure and 15min to the runbook acceptance criteria. 

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Platform Operations, Redwood Inference

- Our colo pair is within the same region (primary/secondary in same metro) so latency should be under 2ms for the mirror—good signal.
